# CSRNG Register Interface Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the memory-mapped register interface for the CSRNG block. It behaves as an AHB-Lite slave and provides software access to the control, status, interrupt, alert, and debug registers of the CSRNG function. The register data width is fixed at 32 bits, while the AHB data bus width is configurable at instantiation time.

The module is responsible for:

- Decoding AHB-Lite read and write transactions.
- Updating software-writable registers and presenting their values to the CSRNG hardware.
- Returning current values from hardware-maintained, read-only, and status registers.
- Enforcing write-protection and byte-lane access rules.
- Reporting bus access errors transactionally.
- Reporting integrity-check failures as a sticky, alert-class output.

## 2. Bus Transaction Behavior

The module shall accept AHB-Lite transactions that address the implemented register map. Every transaction shall complete with either an OKAY or ERROR response. Failed transactions shall not change any register state and shall not generate hardware-visible write or read side effects.

### 2.1 Read Behavior

- Reads from read/write registers shall return the current register value.
- Reads from read-only status registers shall return the latest value supplied by the CSRNG hardware.
- Reads from write-only registers shall return zero.
- Reads from volatile, hardware-supplied registers shall return the current value supplied by hardware at the time of the read.
- Reserved or unimplemented bits shall read as zero.

### 2.2 Write Behavior

- Writes to read/write registers shall update the writable fields using the supplied write data and byte-lane qualifiers.
- Writes to write-only command or test registers shall pass the written data to the hardware and generate a hardware write indication.
- Writes to read-only registers shall be ignored and shall not cause an error response.
- Writes to reserved addresses shall be ignored unless the device-mode configuration causes them to be treated as errors.

### 2.3 Error Behavior

A transaction shall be terminated with an ERROR response and shall not affect register state in the following cases:

1. The transaction addresses a location outside the implemented register map, and the device-mode configuration input is asserted.
2. A write transaction does not include all byte lanes required by the addressed register.

If the device-mode configuration input is deasserted, accesses to unmapped addresses shall return zero on reads and have no effect on writes, and shall not produce an error response.

Read transactions do not have byte-lane restrictions. Reads from any implemented address shall return the appropriate 32-bit register value, including zero for write-only and reserved locations.

### 2.4 Byte-Lane Policy

The module shall require writes to cover every byte lane that contains at least one software-writable bit in the addressed register.

- A register with writable bits only in byte 0 may be written with a byte, halfword, or word access that includes byte 0.
- A register with writable bits in bytes 0 and 1 requires both byte lanes to be selected.
- A fully 32-bit writable register requires all four byte lanes to be selected.
- Writes that omit a required byte lane shall be rejected with an ERROR response.
- Writes that include additional byte lanes beyond the minimum required are accepted; only the implemented fields are affected.

## 3. Register Map

The following table describes the software-visible register set. Reset values apply to all storage elements in this module. Hardware-supplied volatile registers do not have reset values in this module.

| Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interrupt status | W1C | 0x0 | Interrupt event status. Bit 0: command request done. Bit 1: entropy request. Bit 2: hardware instance exception. Bit 3: fatal error. Hardware sets these bits; software writes 1 to a bit to clear it. |
| Interrupt enable | RW | 0x0 | Interrupt enable controls. Bits 0–3 correspond to the interrupt status bits. |
| Interrupt test | WO | Read as 0 | Software writes bit 0–3 to inject an interrupt test event. Reads return zero. |
| Alert test | WO | Read as 0 | Software writes bit 0 to trigger a recoverable alert test and bit 1 to trigger a fatal alert test. Reads return zero. |
| Register write enable | W0C | 0x1 | Write-protection lock bit. Writing 0 clears it; writing 1 has no effect. While cleared, writes to the control register and the error-code test register are ignored. Only reset restores it to 1. |
| Control | RW | 0x0999 | Control fields. Bits 3:0: enable. Bits 7:4: software application enable. Bits 11:8: read internal state. Each field resets to 0x9. Writes are gated by the register write enable lock. |
| Command request | WO | Read as 0 | 32-bit command request word. A legal write passes the value to hardware and signals a new command request. Reads return zero. |
| Software command status | RO | 0x1 | Command status. Bit 0: command ready, resets to 1. Bit 1: command status, resets to 0. Hardware updates both bits. |
| Generated-bits valid | RO, volatile | Hardware supplied | Bit 0: generated bits valid. Bit 1: generated bits FIPS mode. Reads return current hardware state and signal the read to hardware. |
| Generated bits | RO, volatile | Hardware supplied | 32-bit generated random bits. Reads return the current hardware value and signal the read to hardware. |
| Internal state number | RW | 0x0 | Selects the internal state to read back. A legal write notifies hardware of the new selection. |
| Internal state value | RO, volatile | Hardware supplied | 32-bit internal state value selected by the internal state number. Reads return the current hardware value and signal the read to hardware. |
| Hardware exception status | W0C | 0x0 | 16-bit exception status set by hardware. Software clears a bit by writing 0 to it; writing 1 leaves it unchanged. |
| Recoverable alert status | W0C | 0x0 | Recoverable alert status bits at bit positions 0, 1, 2, 3, 12, and 13. Hardware sets these bits. Software clears a bit by writing 0; writing 1 leaves it unchanged. |
| Error code | RO | 0x0 | Error-code status bits set by hardware. Bits indicate FIFO, state-machine, and integrity error conditions. Software cannot modify them. |
| Error-code test | RW | 0x0 | Five error-code test bits. Writes are gated by the register write enable lock. A legal write updates the value and notifies hardware. |
| Main state-machine state | RO | 0x4E | 8-bit current state of the main CSRNG state machine, supplied by hardware. |

## 4. Access Type Semantics

The module shall implement the following access semantics:

- **RW**: The register is readable and writable by software.
- **RO**: The register is readable; software writes are ignored.
- **WO**: The register is writable; reads return zero.
- **W1C**: Write 1 to clear. Software writes a 1 to a bit to clear it. Writes of 0 have no effect.
- **W0C**: Write 0 to clear. Software writes a 0 to a bit to clear it. Writes of 1 have no effect.

For W1C and W0C fields, hardware may set the corresponding status bits asynchronously to software access. The module shall apply the software clear operation only to the bits explicitly written with the required value.

## 5. Write Protection

The module implements a software-writable lock bit that resets to the unlocked state.

- When the lock bit is set, writes to the control register and the error-code test register are accepted.
- When the lock bit is cleared, writes to those two registers are ignored.
- The lock bit itself can be cleared by software but cannot be set by software after it has been cleared.
- The lock bit is not gated by itself; software may write to it regardless of its current state.

## 6. Read Indications to Hardware

For volatile, hardware-supplied registers, a legal read shall return the current hardware-provided value and shall also signal to hardware that the read occurred. Hardware may use this indication to advance or update the data presented to software.

For write-only trigger registers, a legal write shall present the written data to hardware and generate a hardware write indication. This applies to:

- Interrupt test writes.
- Alert test writes.
- Command request writes.
- Internal state number writes.
- Error-code test writes.

## 7. Reset Behavior

When reset is asserted, the module shall:

- Clear all software-accessible storage fields to their reset values.
- Set the register write enable lock to its reset value, so write-protected registers are initially writable.
- Clear any sticky integrity error output.
- Return all read paths to their reset state.
- Not reset hardware-supplied volatile registers, because those values are owned by the CSRNG hardware.

## 8. Integrity Checking

The module shall monitor its internal register write-enable decoding. If a valid register write produces more than one active write-enable at the same time, the module shall assert the integrity error output.

This integrity error output shall be sticky: once asserted, it shall remain asserted until reset. It is not cleared by subsequent accesses and is not affected by normal bus access errors.

Normal bus access errors, such as unmapped addresses or rejected byte-lane combinations, are transactional and shall not cause the sticky integrity output to be asserted.

## 9. Summary of Required Behavior

The module must provide a robust, deterministic AHB-Lite register interface for software to control and observe the CSRNG block. It must enforce the documented access rules, protect privileged control fields when locked, return accurate status and hardware data, and report invalid access conditions appropriately.

A legal access shall complete normally and may update state or generate a hardware indication. An illegal access shall produce an error response without modifying state or generating hardware side effects. Integrity failures shall produce a separate, persistent alert indication.

# Behavioral Specification: Entropy Source Register Interface

## 1. Overview

This module provides the register access layer for the entropy source block. It operates as an AHB-Lite slave and gives software read and write access to a fixed set of 32-bit registers. It also provides the hardware side of the register interface: values written by software are made available to the entropy source logic, and status or data values produced by the entropy source logic are returned to software on reads.

The module does not implement entropy generation, health testing, or alert handling itself. It only performs register address decoding, access validation, read/write data steering, resetting of internal register storage, and integrity-error reporting.

## 2. AHB-Lite Access Behavior

The module shall support AHB-Lite read and write transactions to a 32-bit register map.

For every access:

- The low-order address bits shall be decoded as an offset into the register map.
- A read shall return the current value of the addressed register, or zero for write-only registers and unimplemented/reserved fields.
- A write shall update only the addressed register. Write data for reserved or unimplemented bit positions shall have no effect.
- The module shall not insert wait states for internal register-busy conditions. Register accesses shall be completed without a busy indication.

The module shall support a parameterizable AHB data width, including 64-bit AHB data buses. The register payload is 32 bits, so only the byte lanes corresponding to the addressed register are used.

## 3. Register Access Semantics

Register fields use the following access classes:

- **RO**: read-only. Software cannot change the value.
- **RW**: read/write. Software can read and write the value.
- **W1C**: write-one-to-clear. Software writes a 1 to clear the bit; writing 0 has no effect.
- **W0C**: write-zero-to-clear. Software writes a 0 to clear the bit; writing 1 has no effect.
- **WO / pulse**: write-only or write-pulse behavior. Reads return zero. Writes pass the written value and a write qualifier to the hardware side.

Reserved bit positions shall read as 0. Writes to reserved bit positions are ignored.

## 4. Error Behavior

### 4.1 Undefined Offsets

An offset is considered undefined if it does not correspond to any implemented register.

- If the device-mode input is asserted, an access to an undefined offset shall return an AHB error response.
- If the device-mode input is deasserted, an access to an undefined offset shall not return an error. A read shall return zero and a write shall have no effect.

### 4.2 Byte-Enable Violations

The module shall validate the byte qualifiers of every write access. If a write does not enable all byte lanes required by the addressed register, the module shall:

- return an AHB error response,
- not update any register state,
- and assert the integrity-error output as described in Section 7.

### 4.3 Writes to Read-Only or Locked Registers

A write to a read-only register, or to a register whose write-protection lock is deasserted, shall not modify the register value. Such a write shall be reported on the integrity-error output because no valid register write qualifier is produced. The AHB-Lite response for such a write is not itself an error unless another error condition, such as a byte-enable violation, is also present.

## 5. Reset State

On assertion and release of the active-low reset:

- All internal register storage shall be initialized to its defined reset value.
- The latched integrity-error flag shall be cleared.
- Registers whose values are supplied by the hardware side shall take the reset values provided by the hardware side.

Defined reset values include:

| Register(s) | Reset value |
|---|---|
| Interrupt state | 0x0 |
| Interrupt enable | 0x0 |
| Lock and software-update registers | 0x1 |
| Module enable | 0x9 |
| Configuration fields | 0x9 for the four 4-bit enable/scope fields, 0x0 for the 2-bit selector |
| Entropy control | 0x9 for both 4-bit fields |
| Health test windows | 0x200 and 0x60 |
| Alert threshold | 0x0002 and 0xFFFD |
| Observe FIFO threshold | 0x20 |
| Error-code test | 0x0 |
| Main state machine state | 0xF5 |

Registers whose readback comes from hardware, such as watermarks, total failure counters, FIFO depths, debug status, and error-code status, shall reflect the hardware-supplied values after reset.

## 6. Register Map and Behavioral Requirements

### 6.1 Interrupt Registers

**Interrupt State**

This register reports interrupt status. Each implemented bit is set by the hardware side and cleared by software writing 1. Software writing 0 has no effect. It resets to 0.

**Interrupt Enable**

This register contains read/write interrupt enable bits. Software can set or clear each bit. The value is provided to the hardware side. It resets to 0.

**Interrupt Test**

This is a write-only test register. A read returns zeros. A software write passes the written bit values and a write qualifier to the hardware side so that the hardware can generate interrupt test behavior.

**Alert Test**

This is a write-only test register. A read returns zeros. A software write passes the written bit values and a write qualifier to the hardware side so that recoverable or fatal alert test behavior can be generated.

### 6.2 Lock and Software-Update Registers

**Module Enable Lock**

This is a write-zero-to-clear register. It resets to 1. Software writing 0 clears it; writing 1 is ignored. While this lock is 0, writes to the module-enable register shall be ignored and reported on the integrity-error output.

**Software Update Register**

This is a write-zero-to-clear register. It resets to 1. Software writing 0 clears it; writing 1 is ignored. Its current value is provided to the hardware side.

**Hardware Register Lock**

This is a read-only register. Its value is supplied by the hardware side and resets to 1. While this lock is 0, writes to most configuration, threshold, and control registers are blocked. A write to a locked register is ignored and is reported on the integrity-error output.

### 6.3 Revision

The revision register is read-only and returns constant values: ABI revision 0x03, hardware revision 0x03, and chip type 0x01.

### 6.4 Module Configuration

**Module Enable**

This read/write register resets to 0x9. Software writes are honored only while the module-enable lock is 1.

**Configuration**

This read/write register contains the entropy configuration fields. It resets as defined in Section 5. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Entropy Control**

This read/write register contains entropy routing and type fields. It resets to 0x99. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

### 6.5 Entropy Data

**Entropy Data**

This is a read-only register. The data value is supplied by the hardware side. A read returns the current value and also produces a read qualifier to the hardware side.

### 6.6 Health Test Window and Threshold Registers

**Health Test Windows**

This read/write register contains two 16-bit window values. It resets to 0x200 and 0x60. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Threshold Registers**

The repetition count, adaptive proportion, bucket, Markov, and external health test threshold registers are software-writeable read/write registers. Each contains FIPS and bypass threshold fields. Their readback values are supplied by the hardware side. Software write qualifiers are forwarded to the hardware side. Writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Watermark Registers**

The watermark registers are read-only. Their values are supplied by the hardware side.

**Total Failure Count Registers**

The total failure count registers are read-only. Their 32-bit values are supplied by the hardware side.

### 6.7 Alert Threshold and Failure Counters

**Alert Threshold**

This read/write register contains the alert threshold and its inverted copy. It resets to 0x0002 and 0xFFFD. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Alert Summary and Per-Test Failure Counts**

These registers are read-only. Their values are supplied by the hardware side.

### 6.8 Firmware Override Interface

**Firmware Override Control**

This read/write register contains firmware override mode and entropy insert fields. It resets to 0x99. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Firmware Override SHA3 Start**

This read/write register resets to 0x9. Software writes are not gated by the hardware register lock.

**Firmware Override Write FIFO Full**

This is a read-only status register supplied by the hardware side.

**Firmware Override Read FIFO Overflow**

This is a write-zero-to-clear status register. The hardware side can set the bit. Software writing 0 clears it; writing 1 is ignored.

**Firmware Override Read Data**

This is a read-only register. A read returns the data value supplied by the hardware side and produces a read qualifier to the hardware side.

**Firmware Override Write Data**

This is a write-only data register. A read returns zeros. A software write forwards the 32-bit data value and a write qualifier to the hardware side.

### 6.9 Observe FIFO

**Observe FIFO Threshold**

This is a read/write register. It resets to 0x20. Software writes are honored only while the hardware register lock is 1.

**Observe FIFO Depth**

This is a read-only register. Its value is supplied by the hardware side.

### 6.10 Debug and Status Registers

**Debug Status**

This is a read-only register. All fields are supplied by the hardware side. Unassigned bit positions read as 0.

**Recoverable Alert Status**

This is a write-zero-to-clear status register. The hardware side sets the status bits. Software writing 0 clears the corresponding bits; writing 1 is ignored.

**Error Code**

This is a read-only status register. All bits are supplied by the hardware side.

**Error Code Test**

This is a read/write register. It resets to 0. Software writes update the readable value and also provide the written value and a write qualifier to the hardware side.

**Main State Machine State**

This is a read-only register. Its 9-bit value is supplied by the hardware side. It resets to 0xF5.

## 7. Integrity Monitoring

The module shall monitor every software write to a mapped register offset. A valid write shall produce exactly one write qualifier for the addressed register.

The module shall assert the integrity-error output when a mapped write operation does not produce exactly one valid write qualifier. This includes, but is not limited to:

- a write to a read-only register,
- a write to a register whose write-protection lock is deasserted,
- a write rejected because of a byte-enable violation,
- a write that would produce multiple register write qualifiers due to an internal decode fault.

An access to an undefined offset is not considered a write-enable integrity error.

Once the integrity-error output is asserted, it shall remain asserted until reset. The integrity-error flag is not software-clearable and shall not, by itself, prevent subsequent register accesses from completing.
